description: National investigations into the shadow market for sovereign compute escalate into cross-border legal actions, with several EU member states indicting firms and researchers for circumventing usage controls on public infrastructure. This triggers a political crisis over the integrity of the InvestAI program and forces the Commission to consider emergency audits or compute usage caps, fracturing the internal consensus on open research access.

The emergent AI worker syndicate, first noted in turn 8, expands its influence beyond research labs into public-sector AI deployment teams and independent model auditing collectives. It begins coordinating strikes and work-to-rules around model validation and deployment approvals, effectively slowing down high-stakes AI integration in critical services. Governments face a new form of labour resistance not from displaced workers but from those tasked with managing the systems themselves.
